index.html:43-68 — Bottom nav buttons (.nav-item) lack role='tab' or aria-current='page' for screen readers to announce active state.
index.html:43-68 — Bottom nav <nav> has no aria-label to identify it among multiple landmarks (e.g. 'Main navigation').
index.html:22 — .drawer-close has aria-label='Close' but no aria-expanded state on the toggle (menuBtn) to communicate drawer state.
index.html:30 — .menu-btn has aria-label='Open menu' but no aria-controls or aria-expanded to link it to the drawer it toggles.
index.html:34 — .theme-toggle has aria-label='Toggle theme' but no aria-pressed or text indicating current theme (dark/light).
styles.css:1736 — Focus-visible outline uses 2px solid teal; no fallback for forced-colors/high-contrast mode (Windows HC).
styles.css:1748 — Interactive elements have user-select:none which prevents long-press text selection; may conflict with accessibility text-copy needs.
index.html:44-68 — No skip-link or bypass mechanism before nav; keyboard users must tab through all 6 nav items to reach main content.
styles.css:347-351 — .inactive class uses opacity:0.55 and color muted; no pointer-events:none or aria-disabled, so inactive controls are still focusable/operable.

styles.css:1440-1443 — .fab.hidden uses opacity:0 and transform:scale(0.8); pointer-events:none is present (good) but the element remains in tab order when visible-only via opacity — ensure it's also display:none or visibility:hidden when hidden.

styles.css:1819-1821 — .drawer-overlay.hidden uses display:none (good for a11y); however .drawer.hidden also uses display:none which removes it from tab order — confirm focus is trapped inside the drawer when open.

styles.css:1743-1745 — :focus:not(:focus-visible) removes outline for mouse users; acceptable but relies on browser focus-visible support which may be inconsistent on older Android browsers (target: Android 11).

index.html:44-68 — Nav items use emoji glyphs (🏠, 💵, 📋, 🛒, 🔔, 📊) as sole visual identifier inside <span>; screen readers announce these inconsistently and there is no visually-hidden text label supplementing the icon-only content.
